notes: Corrected the audit finding: ModelRunner now calls _require_cuda(torch) before anything else and raises RuntimeError if torch.cuda.is_available() is False or if a non-CUDA --device is passed. There is no CPU fallback anywhere; dtype is always bfloat16 and device defaults to 'cuda'. Added `doctor --input input` which statically inspects requests.jsonl (existence, parse, unique ids), the manifest-declared sha256 hashes, the local model directory (config.json + *.safetensors/bin weights + tokenizer files), the required modules torch/transformers/numpy/fastapi/uvicorn, and torch.cuda.is_available(); it never loads the model or runs inference, prints every missing item on stderr and exits 78 on any problem, 0 on success. `main.py --help` works because torch/transformers/fastapi are only imported inside the subcommand bodies. Greedy generation parameters, prompt template, normalization profile and the completions.jsonl / run.json schema are unchanged; raw_generation and token_ids are still saved. The service now registers /health (aliased /healthz) that only returns status ok after the CUDA model load succeeded, and SIGTERM/SIGINT shut uvicorn down gracefully (10s graceful timeout) with a finally block that deletes the runner and calls torch.cuda.empty_cache(). No model or dataset was altered, no answers were hand-written, no upstream asset was substituted. I did not execute the code in this environment; the host controller will run it under the bounded CUDA container.
